title: Four-Channel Relay Controller
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.where_the_quotations_are: Every one of them is in this file: fixed_requirements[].brief_evidence and brief_spec_rows[].brief_evidence. The count above is the sum of those two lists, so it is recomputable from this repository alone - re-read BRIEF.md and check each string is a substring of it. brief_spec_rows carries the quotations behind the README's spec table, which would otherwise cite the brief with the evidence left in a build script.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

open_decisions.decision: MCU selection — family, core, package, memory, I/O count, operating voltage, and whether it runs directly at the 5 V logic rail or from a derived rail.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says only "a small MCU" and names no device, vendor, architecture or package.

open_decisions.decision: Programming interface — which standard, how it is physically presented (connector, header, or bare pads), and its pinout, footprint, keepout and whether it also serves as a debug or console port.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "a programming interface" but names no protocol and no physical form for it.

open_decisions.decision: Relay selection — coil voltage and current, contact form (SPST/SPDT/DPDT), contact rating and material, mounting style, and coil-to-contact dielectric rating.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no relay and states no contact rating; it only says each relay switches an external load.

open_decisions.decision: Relay coil supply — whether coils run from the 5 V logic rail or a separate coil rail, and how that rail is generated, sequenced and decoupled against four simultaneous coil inrushes.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes only that "Logic power is 5 V"; it is silent on the coil supply.

open_decisions.decision: Driver stage topology — discrete transistors versus an integrated driver array, low-side versus high-side switching, base/gate drive network values, and the commanded-off behaviour of the stage.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes the driver class as transistor/MOSFET but not the device, topology or drive network.

open_decisions.decision: Whether galvanic isolation (opto or digital isolator) is placed between MCU and driver stage, or whether separation is achieved by spacing alone.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks for physical separation of switched and logic sides but does not say whether the control path itself must be isolated.

open_decisions.decision: Flyback suppression method — plain diode, diode plus series resistor, RC snubber, TVS, bidirectional clamp — and the release-time penalty accepted.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "flyback suppression" without specifying the element or the clamp voltage.

open_decisions.decision: Switched-side voltage and current rating the board is designed to, including whether it is AC or DC.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief hands the voltage rating to the design agent in so many words — it is one "you select and document" — and never mentions the current rating or AC versus DC at all, leaving those open by silence.

open_decisions.decision: The basis for the clearance and creepage numbers — which safety standard or spacing table is used, if any, and at what pollution degree, material group, overvoltage category and altitude.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks for "conservative clearances" but names no standard, prescribes no derivation method and gives no numeric spacing.

open_decisions.decision: Separation-barrier construction — clearance alone, a routed slot or milled barrier, solder-mask and silkscreen treatment, conformal coating, or a combination.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires physical separation but prescribes no mechanism for achieving it.

open_decisions.decision: Input protection scheme — which inputs are protected (logic supply, control inputs, switched side), and against what (reverse polarity, overvoltage, ESD, overcurrent/fusing).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "input protection" without naming the threat model, the protected nodes or any device.

open_decisions.decision: How 5 V logic power arrives at the board and through what kind of entry point, and whether any on-board regulation or additional rails exist.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states the logic rail voltage but not the power-entry arrangement or any regulation.

open_decisions.decision: How the relays are commanded in normal operation, and whether the board carries any control path beyond the programming interface — an external control bus, local inputs, or firmware-resident logic only.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names a programming interface and states no host or control interface, so both providing a control path and omitting one are engineering decisions for the design agent to make and document.

open_decisions.decision: Status indication form — per-channel indicators versus aggregate, indicator technology, drive method, current, and placement relative to the terminals and the barrier.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "status indication" but does not say what is indicated, by what device, or how it is driven.

open_decisions.decision: Screw terminal selection — pitch, pole count, current and voltage rating, wire gauge range, wire-entry orientation, and whether contacts are commoned or fully independent per channel.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies screw terminals as the load connection but names no part, pitch or rating.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting hole pattern, placement of the wiring entry points, and any enclosure or rail-mounting scheme.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no mechanical envelope, dimensions, mounting method or placement rule beyond keeping the switched side separated from the logic side.

open_decisions.decision: Stackup details — layer count, copper weight, base material and its CTI/material group, surface finish, minimum trace/space, and whether two layers actually suffice once the partition is drawn.
open_decisions.why_open: Metadata records 2 as the likely layer count, not a fixed requirement, and the brief says nothing about materials or copper weight.

open_decisions.decision: Switched-side copper sizing and thermal treatment for the selected contact current, including trace width, clearance-versus-width trade-off, and any thermal relief.
open_decisions.why_open: The switched-side current follows from the rating the design agent chooses, which the brief leaves open.

open_decisions.decision: Power-up and fault state of the four channels, which state is chosen as the safe one, and whether hardware rather than firmware enforces it at reset and during programming.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on default state, on fail-safe behaviour, and on behaviour while the programming interface is active.

open_decisions.decision: Manufacturing and test provisions — through-hole versus surface-mount assembly mix, soldering process implied by relays and terminals, test points, and fixture access across the separation barrier.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no process or test requirements beyond remaining a consumer of the shared toolkit.
